title: Is the Furbo 360 Dog Camera Worth It in 2026?
metaDescription: Is the Furbo 360 worth $200 plus subscription fees? We break down motorized tracking, treat flinging, Furbo Nanny costs, and free tier limits.
h1: Is the Furbo 360 Dog Camera worth it in 2026?
dek: With a $200 hardware price tag and an optional $69-per-year cloud subscription, the Furbo 360 is a major investment. Here is an unvarnished look at what works, what annoys owners, and whether it justifies the steep premium over basic security cameras.
coverAlt: Furbo 360 dog camera on a living room console table tossing a treat to a dog
bodyHtml:
The Furbo 360 Dog Camera is easily the most recognized pet gadget on the market. With its sleek white hourglass silhouette, natural bamboo lid, and headline feature of flinging treats across the room from your smartphone, it promises complete peace of mind while you are away from home. However, with an initial hardware price tag hovering around $200 and an optional $69-per-year cloud subscription required to unlock its best features, buying a Furbo is a serious financial commitment compared to a standard $35 indoor security camera.

Whether the Furbo 360 is genuinely worth that premium depends heavily on your dog's temperament and your tolerance for cloud subscriptions. If your dog suffers from separation anxiety, paces through multiple rooms, or requires structured crate training rewards, the Furbo offers specialized acoustic intelligence and motorized tracking that generic security cameras cannot match. But if you simply want a quick visual check-in on a sleeping pet, it is easy to overspend. This review breaks down real-world hardware performance, treat dispensing mechanics, and the true two-year cost of ownership. For comparative context, review our Furbo vs Petcube comparison, our guide to the top 7 pet cameras reviewed, and the Pet Supplies hub.

Who should skip the Furbo 360

  • Subscription-averse buyers: Skip the Furbo if you refuse to pay an ongoing $69 per year for cloud video recording and AI smart alerts; a 2K camera with local microSD storage is a much smarter financial choice.
  • Cat-only households: Skip this model; cats are better served by specialized cat monitors featuring laser pointers or feather wands rather than a heavy kibble tosser.
  • Strict budget shoppers: Skip if your spending limit is under $50; plenty of dependable pan-and-tilt security cameras cover room monitoring without treat mechanics.

What it is and who it targets

The Furbo 360 is a dedicated smart indoor pet monitor combining a 1080p camera, a motorized 360-degree rotating base, full-duplex two-way audio, and a motorized treat-tossing catapult. Unlike general home security cameras designed to catch burglars, Furbo's hardware and software are tuned specifically to canine habits. It targets dog owners dealing with daytime separation anxiety, crate training, or noise complaints from apartment neighbors. Its primary job is twofold: alert you to canine distress before destructive habits form, and let you intervene remotely with soothing voice audio and edible rewards.

Specs that matter

What owners praise about the Furbo 360

  • Accurate separation anxiety alerts: Owners of vocal dogs consistently praise the sound classification algorithms. Furbo reliably differentiates between a single doorbell bark, continuous alarm barking, and mournful separation howling, sending timely smartphone notifications before neighbors complain.
  • Motorized auto-tracking follows pacing pets: The 360-degree rotating base turns quietly and smoothly to follow dogs moving between room corners, keeping active pets centered in the frame.
  • Color night vision provides vital context: Preserving color in low ambient light lets you quickly see whether your dog is gnawing on an approved chew toy or chewing upholstery fabric without harsh infrared glare.
  • Effective remote training reward: The treat catapult flings kibble 2 to 4 feet across the carpet, turning daytime check-ins into positive reinforcement sessions for crate-trained puppies.

What owners complain about

  • Heavy subscription dependency: Many buyers feel blindsided after discovering that automated dog tracking, cloud event video history, and specialized emergency alerts require the paid Furbo Nanny subscription ($69/year).
  • Strict treat size requirements: The internal carousel is unforgiving. Soft, moist, or crumbly treats break apart into greasy residue that jams the dispensing gears, requiring complete manual disassembly to clean.
  • No local microSD backup: The device lacks a physical memory card slot. If your home Wi-Fi drops offline or cloud servers experience downtime, video recording ceases entirely.

The 2-year cost math: Hardware + Furbo Nanny breakdown

Before entering credit card details, calculate the full 24-month ownership equation. The Furbo 360 sells for approximately $200 at retail. While live streaming, manual two-way intercom audio, and manual treat tossing function completely free out of the box, accessing recorded cloud video history, automated 360 pet tracking, and specialized howling alerts requires the Furbo Nanny subscription ($6.99/month or $69/year). Over two years, hardware ($200) plus two years of Nanny ($138) brings your total expenditure to $338.

By contrast, purchasing a standalone 2K pan-and-tilt camera like the Eufy Indoor Cam E220 ($40) paired with a high-endurance 128GB microSD memory card ($15) costs exactly $55 total across two years, delivering continuous local 24/7 video recording with zero monthly subscription fees. If you choose the Furbo 360, you are effectively paying an extra $283 over two years specifically for automated treat tossing, color night vision, and canine acoustic sound classification. For owners managing serious separation anxiety, that premium can save a rental lease; for casual check-ins, it is an expensive luxury.

Two alternatives to consider before buying

  • For zero ongoing subscription fees: The Eufy Indoor Cam E220 costs around $40, offers sharper 2K resolution, motorized 360 pan and tilt, and stores continuous video on an inexpensive local microSD card with no monthly bills. (Trade-off: no treat tossing).
  • For high-capacity treat dispensing & wall mounting: The Petcube Bites 2 Lite costs roughly $100 less upfront, holds three times more treats (1.5 lbs), features a dishwasher-safe hopper, and mounts securely to drywall out of reach of large dogs. (Trade-off: stationary fixed lens).

Verdict: Should you buy the Furbo 360?

The Verdict · $$$$

Furbo 360° Dog Camera

In a suburban living room where a young rescue Australian Shepherd paces between the entryway and the living room rug, whining whenever neighbors walk down the hall, a generic security camera only sends generic noise pings. The Furbo 360 steps in as a specialized behavioral intervention tool. Its motorized 360 rotating base tracks the dog as they pace from sofa to doorway, while its canine sound algorithms distinguish between a single warning bark and escalating separation distress howling. Opening the phone app, issuing a calm verbal cue, and launching two crunchy training treats provides an immediate dopamine reset, breaking the anxiety loop before destructive chewing begins.

However, that peace of mind comes with strict mechanical and financial caveats. The internal flinging carousel demands uniform, dry, circular kibble under 0.5 inches in diameter; loading greasy training jerky or crumbly raw biscuits causes sticky clogs that require taking the device apart with screwdrivers to clear. Furthermore, automated tracking, cloud video clip history, and distinct howling alerts are gated behind the $69-per-year Furbo Nanny subscription. Without it, you are left with live streaming and manual treat tossing, making the $200 hardware feel steep unless you fully embrace the paid ecosystem.

Pros

  • Smooth 360-degree motorized tracking follows restless pets
  • Color night vision delivers exceptional low-light clarity
  • Specialized acoustic detection for howling, crying, and smoke alarms
  • Effective remote treat tossing mechanism with satisfying range
  • Sleek furniture-grade aesthetic with real bamboo lid

Cons

  • Expensive $200 hardware price point ($338 total over 2 years with Nanny)
  • Full video history and auto-tracking require Furbo Nanny ($69/yr)
  • No physical microSD card slot for offline local recording
  • Treat hopper only accepts dry, crunchy treats under 0.5 inches

Buy the Furbo 360 if you have an anxious or active dog, value specialized howling and distress alerts, and are comfortable paying for the Furbo Nanny subscription to unlock full tracking and video history. Skip it if you only want occasional visual check-ins on a calm pet or refuse to pay annual cloud storage fees.

Our research methodology

Nobody at Pickora ran a closed commercial testing lab. Our product audit synthesizes manufacturer electrical and mechanical schematics, published benchmark evaluations from independent tech reviewers (including PCMag, CNET, and Wirecutter), and verified multi-month canine owner reliability reports through November 2026. We examine treat dispensing reliability, acoustic detection accuracy, Wi-Fi connectivity stability, and the true cost of subscription tiers to give you transparent buying guidance.

faq.q: Can you use the Furbo 360 Dog Camera without paying for the Furbo Nanny subscription?
faq.a: Yes. The basic camera functions—including 1080p live streaming, manual two-way voice audio, manual treat tossing, and real-time barking notifications—work free of charge. However, recorded cloud video clips, automated 360 pet tracking, and specialized howling/emergency alerts require an active Furbo Nanny subscription.

faq.q: What happens to the Furbo 360 if your home internet or Wi-Fi goes down?
faq.a: Because the Furbo 360 lacks a physical microSD card slot or internal offline storage, it cannot record video or send notifications during an internet outage. Once your home Wi-Fi connection is restored, the camera automatically reconnects to cloud servers and resumes normal monitoring.

faq.q: How much does the Furbo Nanny subscription cost per month and per year?
faq.a: The Furbo Nanny service costs $6.99 per month when billed monthly, or $69 per year when billed annually (roughly $5.75 per month). Furbo typically includes a 3-month free trial with new hardware purchases, after which billing renews automatically unless canceled.

faq.q: What kind of treats work best in the Furbo 360 without causing motor jams?
faq.a: Use firm, dry, circular crunchy treats measuring between 0.3 and 0.5 inches in diameter (such as standard training kibble or freeze-dried meat pellets). Never load soft, sticky, crumbly, or irregularly shaped treats like jerky or cheese, as they quickly gum up the internal dispensing carousel.

faq.q: Is the Furbo 360 durable enough to survive a large dog knocking it over?
faq.a: The Furbo features a weighted base, a spill-resistant bamboo lid, and includes strong 3M double-sided adhesive pads to anchor it to smooth tables. However, a determined 70-pound dog experiencing severe anxiety can swat it off a low coffee table. For heavy dogs, place the unit on a high shelf or credenza at least 4.5 to 5 feet off the floor.
